distributorInventory.title: Distributor inventory days
distributorInventory.content:
Distributor inventory days is how many days of forward sell-through the channel is holding, before any of it has been sold to an end customer.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: this is the key swing factor in the 2023-2025 downcycle. Distributors massively over-ordered during the 2021-2022 chip shortage, then stopped ordering almost entirely to work the excess off -- days peaked near 43 in early FY2025 and has been correcting back toward MCHP's historical ~30-day norm since. Reported revenue lags real end-demand by a quarter or more while this number is moving.

What to watch:

  • Days falling toward the ~25-30 day normal range -- the signal that destocking is over and reported revenue can track sell-through again
  • A renewed rise, which would mean distributors are over-ordering again, not that demand improved

productMix.title: Revenue by product line
productMix.content:
Microchip splits revenue across three product lines: Analog, Microcontrollers (MCU) and Other products (FPGAs, memory and licensing).

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: microcontrollers are the larger, higher-margin franchise and the one most exposed to the industrial and automotive end markets hit hardest by distributor destocking; Analog has recovered faster. The relative pace of each line's recovery is a better read on underlying demand than consolidated revenue alone.

What to watch:

  • Microcontrollers reclaiming share of the mix as the downcycle ends
  • Whether Analog's recovery is outpacing or lagging MCU

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Microchip Technology Incorporated: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
